name: Bianca Moreau
life: “I still remember hearing a single adult's care obligations discounted.” On Monday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Bianca pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I voted to give the slot to a parent. The single person who lost gets up at four to visit her dad.
appearance: Bianca has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a red windbreaker. It usually goes with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. When somebody else has the floor, Bianca steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Bianca is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Bianca is concerned.
agenda: To let applicants describe obligations beyond parental status.
family: Ismael Fong is Bianca’s cousin. Bianca chooses whether to use it. Ismael saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A room for a father*, Ismael says, “I want to meet him at the gate so my mother can choose when to see him.”
connections: Darcy Wu. A bus pass complicates a panel vote framed entirely around parents who need to drive.

reactions.situation: Someone asks whether the grant might buy a bus pass instead
reactions.response: Bianca prices a usable bus pass before dismissing it as a different kind of grant.
